headline.text: Lapin hyvinvointialue lags nationally in crude curative treatment at 18.5% (95% CI 15.8–21.5; n=131/710) versus 27.0% (4009/14873), with the 95% confidence interval excluding the national value.

details.text: Across overlapping treatment categories, the crude life-prolonging treatment share is 16.1% (95% CI 13.5–18.9; n=114/710) versus 30.4% (4522/14873) nationally, while the crude symptomatic treatment share is 44.5% (95% CI 40.9–48.2; n=316/710) versus 39.5% (5871/14873), with the 95% confidence intervals excluding the national values.

The crude share with no treatment record within 12 months is 33.8% (95% CI 30.4–37.4; n=240/710) compared with 27.5% (4089/14873) nationally, with the 95% confidence interval excluding and sitting above the national value; this category mixes untreated patients and unrecorded treatment.

The crude share with an MDT meeting recorded is 3.0% (95% CI 1.9–4.5; n=21/710) versus 6.0% (893/14873) nationally, with the 95% confidence interval excluding the national value, though HILMO entries come only from direct patient contacts and measure recording practice rather than care.

Nationally, preliminary unpublished figures show lung cancer care takes 155 days on average from symptoms to treatment in Finland versus 107 days in Sweden and 67 days in Denmark, comprising 56 days of patient delay, 41 days in primary care, and 58 days in specialist care.

headline.text: Public registry data leave major uncertainties because county tables report crude shares without age or stage adjustment, cannot separate unrecorded treatment from non-treatment, and omit key pathway timestamps.

details.text: Reading the crude 33.8% (95% CI 30.4–37.4; n=240/710) no-treatment-record share within 12 months—whose 95% confidence interval is above the national 27.5% (4089/14873)—as a data-quality signal indicates that low crude treatment shares may partly reflect unrecorded treatment, whereas a journal article finding about 90% HILMO and Cancer Registry concordance applies only to diagnoses.

Taulukko 11 gives crude county shares that are not age-adjusted—age-adjusted county shares appear only in Kuva 16, where only digitised national curative reference lines of 26.7% for men and 26.9% for women (±0.5 percentage points) are available here—and, as a separate limitation, shares cannot be stage-adjusted because stage at diagnosis is missing for about 48% of patients.

Public report data do not measure symptom onset, referrals, imaging waits (showing only that about 20% of diagnoses rest on clinical examination such as imaging alone), or dates of specialist visits and treatment start, and primary care visits are not included in the report's data while occupational health is not mentioned.

headline.text: The team recommends auditing recording completeness for stage, drug treatment, and MDT coding, reporting access times using THL 21/2016 definitions with handover alerts, and standardising referrals and diagnostic coordination.

details.text: Given Lappi's crude 33.8% (95% CI 30.4–37.4; n=240/710) 12-month no-treatment-record share, crude 3.0% (95% CI 1.9–4.5; n=21/710) MDT-recorded share across overlapping categories, and incomplete national data reporting, the team recommends publishing county recording completeness for stage, drug treatment, and MDT coding while the STM roadmap (measure 3.2.1) plans a national quality registry with an undated 90% coverage indicator including stage.

Because the Health Care Act (§52) sets no maximum time for a cancer suspicion, the team recommends reporting access times from referral to treatment start using THL guidance Ohjaus 21/2016 definitions (covering 16 cancers) and flagging stalled handovers while the STM roadmap (measure 3.1.2) plans national pathways with target access times for five cancers by 2026–2028.

Supported by mentor insight that a weak referral gets a lower urgency rating in specialist care, the team recommends a KYS-style referral template, referring persistent unexplained symptoms after a normal X-ray, and naming a diagnostic-phase contact, while the Filha programme's diagnostics recommendation with primary-care referral criteria is to be carried out before the 2030 mid-term evaluation.

As the team recommends, naming a diagnostic-phase contact person and standardising referrals act early while the STM roadmap plans guidance on a named care-coordinator model by 2026–2028 for county adoption by 2029–2031 without specifying the care phase (measure 1.2.3) and plans standardised referral criteria and symptom-based models by 2026–2028 (measure 2.5.2).

q:4e702a20fe.claim_text: Finland has no unified national system to steer the drafting of cancer-specific treatment recommendations, or the implementation and monitoring of care pathways based on them (quality and effectiveness targets/indicators, including access to care, and cancer-specific and generic PROMs). Existing recommendations and pathways, and the targets and indicators to be monitored, are not coordinated nationally. This maintains regional inequality in the availability and effectiveness of cancer care.
q:4e702a20fe.quote: Suomessa ei ole yhtenäistä kansallista järjestelmää, joka ohjaisi syöpäkohtaisten hoitosuositusten laatimista sekä niihin perustuvien hoitoketjujen toteutusta ja seurantaa (laatu- ja vaikuttavuustavoitteet/indikaattorit, mukaan lukien hoitoonpääsy sekä syöpäkohtaiset ja geneeriset PROM-vointimittarit). Olemassa olevia hoitosuosituksia ja -ketjuja sekä seurattavia tavoitteita ja indikaattoreita ei koordinoida kansallisella tasolla. Tämä ylläpitää alueellista eriarvoisuutta syövän hoidon saatavuudessa ja vaikuttavuudessa.
q:4e702a20fe.quote_en: Finland does not have a uniform national system to guide the preparation of cancer-specific clinical guidelines and the implementation and monitoring of care pathways based on them (quality and effectiveness targets/indicators, including access to care as well as cancer-specific and generic PROM well-being measures). Existing clinical guidelines and care pathways as well as monitored targets and indicators are not coordinated at the national level. This maintains regional inequality in the availability and effectiveness of cancer care.

rec:1.claim_text: Team recommendation 1: Counties report access times using the THL 21/2016 definitions, with handover alerts. Each wellbeing services county reports lung cancer access times (referral → first specialist visit → diagnosis → treatment start) using the definitions in THL's Hoitoonpääsyn seuranta syövän hoidossa (Ohjaus 21/2016). Until national target times exist, flag stalled handovers.
rec:1.location: §1. Counties report access times using the THL 21/2016 definitions, with handover alerts

rec:2.claim_text: Team recommendation 2: A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact. Adopt a standard referral content list and template, modelled on KYS. • Add a rule for primary care: if symptoms persist after a normal X-ray, refer for a pulmonologist assessment. • Name a contact person for the diagnostic phase, from referral to diagnosis.
rec:2.location: §2. A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact

rec:3.claim_text: Team recommendation 3: Report recording completeness per county: stage, drug treatment, MDT coding. Publish, per county, how completely stage, drug treatment and MDT meetings are recorded. Read county ‘gaps’ in these fields as data-quality signals first.
